chunks: From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Khazzaz, from Umar ibn Aban, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

O Abu Hamza, the earth does not remain devoid of a scholar from us; if people increase [in knowledge/religion], he says 'They have increased,' and if they decrease, he says 'They have decreased.' And Allah will not cause that scholar to depart [from the world] until He sees in his offspring one who knows like his knowledge or whatever Allah wills.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition of the earth regarding scholars from the Ahl al-Bayt according to Imam Al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) establishes the doctrine of the 'Daher al-Ilm' (the outwardly known scholar) as a perpetual divine guarantee, ensuring the earth is never devoid of a living authority from the Ahl al-Bayt to guide the community. It highlights the continuity of religious authority through a chain of succession, where the current scholar remains until Allah appoints a successor from his progeny with equal or greater knowledge, a concept central to Shia understanding of the Imamate and the role of the Marja' in the era of the Hidden Imam.
